subject: Sprint-aligned rollover + staged capacity uplift for Acme Health
thread_summary: Acme Health requests a co-term renewal aligned to their fiscal year plus a staged capacity uplift. Sales proposes a 24-month term with a phased ramp and early upsell credits; procurement requests minor termination language edits. Internal approvals obtained for a prepay discount and staged true-up language; Acme requests final DocuSign link.
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2024 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal timing + capacity uplift question

Hi Dylan,

Hope you’re well. We’re starting to plan our FY25 budget and want to discuss the upcoming renewal. Two asks from procurement and product:

- Can we align the renewal to our fiscal year (co-term to 2025-07-01)?
- We expect a usage uplift phased over the next 9 months — can you propose a staged capacity plan (we may ramp from a baseline to ~2.5x by Q3)?

Procurement also prefers a 24-month contract if pricing is reasonable and would like an auto-renew unless we give 60-days notice. Can you send a proposal that covers co-terming + a ramp schedule and highlight any upfront credits or true-up mechanics?

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Health
[Attachment: FY25_ask_summary.pdf (PDF - 120KB)]

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2024 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + capacity uplift question

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a proposal (v3) that aims to balance predictability for Acme with capacity flexibility. High level: 

- Term: 24 months, co-term to Acme fiscal year boundary 2025-07-01 (effective 2024-07-01 -> 2026-06-30).
- Staged ramp (billing & capacity):
  * Months 0–3: baseline = 100% (current committed level)
  * Months 4–9: linear ramp to 175% of baseline (weekly true-ups)
  * Months 10–24: stabilized at 250% of baseline with quarterly true-up windows
- Economics: 15% prepay discount if Acme prepays 12 months at signing; otherwise standard tiered pricing with early-upsell credits applied (credit reduces effective unit price for first 6 months of uplift).
- Auto-renew: proposed auto-renew with 60-day opt-out (we can make the auto-renew opt-out window 90 days on enterprise approval).
- True-up: monthly usage true-up for months 4–9, quarterly thereafter; staged overage protection band for first two true-ups.

Attachments: acme_proposal_v3.pdf (contains SOW, ramp table, pricing model summary).

Marissa / Karthik — looping you for approvals on discount authority and legal on the auto-renew language. Samantha — if this looks directionally okay I’ll send a clean DocuSign package once we land internal approvals.

Next steps I suggest: procurement to confirm target co-term and whether the 15% prepay discount is acceptable, then we’ll hand to legal for redline.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Sales Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme_proposal_v3.pdf (PDF - 320KB)]

Marissa / Karthik — quick internal note. I’ve proposed a 24-mo co-term with a staged ramp and 15% prepay discount. Key asks: 

- Marissa: confirm we can offer 15% on a 12-month upfront for a 24-mo term (we’re absorbing some near-term Lambda/GPU costs on their expected ramp). If not, what’s your recommended floor?
- Karthik: approve auto-renew clause as 60-day opt-out; procurement pushed for auto-renew but wants termination rights if we materially change prices. We should add a carve-out for material adverse performance (SLA credit triggers) and a canary ramp rollback clause if we hit production stability issues.

I’ve attached the proposal and a quick margin sketch — pricing_model.xlsx — please review; need responses by EOD so I can respond to Acme tomorrow.

Thanks,
Dylan

Thanks Dylan — reviewed. Rapid answers: 

- Approve 15% prepay discount on 12-month upfront applied to invoice at signing. That’s within my authority for strategic deals if Legal signs off on termination language.
- Recommend adding a staged true-up clause: first two true-ups are advisory (no financial penalty) provided usage spikes are within the documented ramp plan; after that, standard true-up applies. This protects Acme during onboarding and reduces friction.
- Legal (Karthik) should add: material-change termination right if we change pricing >10% year-over-year or materially change data handling. Add a canary rollback: if a selected percentage of requests (e.g., 5%) experience latency regressions above the SLO for two consecutive weeks, Acme can pause new traffic and revert to previous model variant.

I attached my suggested pricing ladder and a revised clause text in the spreadsheet. If you want broader discount authority, we can escalate to VP Sales but I think 15% is reasonable.

Marissa Cole
VP Sales, Americas
Redwood Inference
